en: The Hymn to the Seven Buddhas:
He who was born in Vandhumatī into the noble family of kings by the name of Vipaśyin,
and whose lifespan as the teacher of gods and men reached eighty thousand years for those who have passed away;

I pay homage to that Lord of Jinas, the ocean of wisdom who has extinguished the entire fire of afflictions, by whom the state of a Victor was attained at the foot of the Potala tree through the power of the Ten Strengths. || 1 ||
He who was born in the great lineage of lords of the earth at that preeminent city, whose lifespan was seventy thousand years, who was a treasury of all virtues, and who,
being skilled in benefiting others, attained awakening at the foot of a *puṇḍarīka* tree— [he is this one].
I pay homage to that Śikhin, the best of sages, a mass of wisdom who has reached the further shore of saṃsāra. (2)
He who was born into a lineage of kings of renowned fame beyond comparison,
whose long-lived wisdom reached sixty thousand years,
and by whom immortality was attained at the foot of the Śāla tree after conquering all afflictions without exception.
I pay homage to that King of Dharma, who brings about the welfare of the world and is named Viśvabhū. || 3 ||
Born in Kṣemāvatī into a lineage of brahmins equal to lords of men, he was a self-controlled master who lived for forty-eight thousand years as a treasury of preeminent virtues;
by him, the Lord of Jinas— which destroys the three worlds— was attained through his sovereignty over the sword of knowledge.
I pay homage to the Sugata of lion-like body, the incomparable Kakupchanda, the Lord of Sages.
In Śobhāvatī, he was born into a lineage of brahmins honored by kings; there, he lived for thirty thousand years with an exceedingly beautiful body.
It was by him that Buddhahood was attained at Udumbara, under the venerable and preeminent Ratnācala tree.
I pay homage to that teacher, the sage Kanakamuni, who has destroyed the darkness of delusion. || 5 ||
Born in Vārāṇasī into a lineage of brahmins honored by the king Kṛṣīśa, he lived for twenty thousand years— an exceedingly venerable lifespan— until,
at the foot of a banyan tree, he nourished the ocean of the three worlds through his divine course.
I pay homage to that venerable one, the faultless and supreme sage Kāśyapa, the protector of the world. || 6 ||
He who was born in the illustrious and vast city of Kapilavastu, within the lineage of the Śākya kings;
he who was the sole kinsman of all the world for one hundred years;
and he by whom, having gone forth at the foot of the Aśvattha tree, supreme enlightenment was attained even over Namuci.
I pay homage to that Lion of the Śākyas, the Buddha, the kinsman of the sun, who is bowed to by gods and men. (7)
Having taken birth in the lineage of Viprati, honored by the best of kings, in Ketumatī,
that treasury of supreme virtues attained Buddhahood at the foot of a Nāga tree;
the lifespan of that Blessed One, which was to be spent for eighty thousand years, will be his foremost [measure].
I pay homage to Maitreyanātha, the future Lord of the World, who dwells in the supreme city of Tuṣita. || 8 ||

Having praised the seven Buddhas who have appeared in their entirety, and having praised Maitreya— the future Lord of the World currently residing in the Tuṣita heaven, radiant with the splendor of forty-nine suns— whatever merit has been generated, which yields the fruit of auspicious rebirth for all embodied beings, [may it be dedicated].
Having severed the bonds of affliction, may he proceed toward nirvāṇa, moving like the sages.
The Praise to the Seven Glorious Buddhas is completed.
